name: Division Threshold — Season 1
generationLine: Finished full-color portrait prestige science-fiction comic page. CHARACTER FIRST: stage every civic, legal, technical and political pressure through what a particular person wants, fears, touches, endures, chooses or refuses. Bodies must feel physically real and materially specific. Organics are living grown persons: warm dermis, humidity, subtle moisture, flexing tissue, mineral/ceramic/keratin transitions, repair gel, abrasion and biological response where appropriate—not robots, armor suits or dry sculptures. Augments remain human flesh with healed scars, pressure marks, sweat, tissue around ports, actuator heat, lubricant and mechanical resistance where appropriate—not superhero armor. Intelligences must have weight, surface wear, thermal presence, contact sound and machine-native material reality without humanizing them. Baselines are equally embodied: skin, breath, fatigue, bruising, fabric and sweat. Preserve tactile surfaces—old concrete, worn polymers, damp service spaces, dust, oil, condensation, metal, glass and fabric. The social commentary is pressure on people, never the visual protagonist. Naturalistic acting, intimate reactions, readable physical geography, no generic cyberpunk neon, no sterile CG gloss, no superhero posing, no encyclopedia-style exposition. Fictional production.
